nodes.statement: The equilibrium model sits on MacArthur & Wilson's crossing rate curves: ensemble-mean richness tracks the analytic S* = P*c/(c+e) across the area gradient (corr 0.992), and species identity turns over ~15x the net change while richness holds.

nodes.label: Both canonical predictions emerge as laws: richness grows with area as a powe...
nodes.statement: Both canonical predictions emerge as laws: richness grows with area as a power law S ~ A^z (z = 0.12) and declines monotonically with isolation (Spearman -0.97) - area acting through extinction, isolation through colonization.

nodes.statement: Hubbell neutral drift also produces a positive species-area relationship (z ~ 0.76 vs equilibrium z ~ 0.13), so the SAR alone cannot discriminate neutral drift from niche-based colonization/extinction - two unrelated mechanisms converge on the same qualitative law.

nodes.statement: The taxa-area relationship holds for microbes but is flatter (z ~ 0.04 vs macro 0.12, ~3x) with ~20x faster turnover, consistent with the empirical microbial taxa-area literature (Horner-Devine 2004; Bell 2005).

nodes.label: Under island ontogeny (area rises then erodes), richness overshoots and then ...
nodes.statement: Under island ontogeny (area rises then erodes), richness overshoots and then declines (peak ~52 at mid-age, falling to ~27): the MacArthur-Wilson equilibrium is transient over geological time, as the General Dynamic Model predicts (Whittaker 2008).

nodes.statement: Coupling the curves via the rescue effect (immigration lowering extinction) raises equilibrium richness (30->37) and damps turnover (30->23 events/gen), reducing exactly to the independent-curves baseline at rescue=0 (Brown & Kodric-Brown 1977).
